title: User Account Created
detection_hypothesis: If an adversary establishes a new foothold identity, the account creation audit record will name the creating subject and the new account.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.SubjectUserName: Account that performed the audited action.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
expected_volume: Low to moderate depending on joiner volume.
false_positive_strategy: Nearly all matches are legitimate provisioning. Value comes from correlating the new account with subsequent privileged group changes and first logon location.
tuning_guidance: Keep the rule at low severity and route it to enrichment rather than to a queue. Exclude only the named provisioning service account.
test_strategy: Positive cases create accounts from two different administrative subjects. Negative cases use the provisioning service, an account deletion, and a password change.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
